data.content_ref: inline:Reformulate the skeptical semantics on an interval lattice: each node's status is a closed interval [lower, upper] of possible commitments, and the grounded extension is the least fixed point of a monotone operator on this lattice. Suspension is then a non-degenerate interval rather than a third diagnostic label, so 'undecided' carries semantic content (the range of commitments consistent with the graph) and determinism follows from the Knaster–Tarski least-fixed-point theorem rather than from enumeration discipline. Criticizable: interval semantics may fail to coincide with grounded extension on graphs with odd attack cycles; widening/abstract-interpretation machinery adds complexity that may exceed polynomial bounds; interaction with attack-defeater warrants (SRC_002) and support chains (SRC_005) is uncharacterized.
